title: Introduce RBAC retention classifier and KMS multipath fallback
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds tenant-configurable RBAC retention classifier and KMS multipath fallback. No customer-facing API changes; operators must add secondary KMS config if they want multipath.
description:
Context: We need deterministic, policy-driven retention buckets for audit events combined with more resilient KMS usage in edge cases where a primary KMS provider experiences transient failures. This PR implements a small RBAC-v2-aligned "retention classifier" that maps requests and resource attributes to one of the configured retention buckets (short/standard/long) and wires audit emitters to include retention metadata. Simultaneously, it adds a KMS multipath fallback shim that can attempt a secondary provider or cached session when the primary KMS returns retriable errors.

Motivation: Several compliance customers requested per-tenant retention annotations for audit logs (so downstream archivers can apply correct retention and deletion policies). Separately, we've observed rare incidents where a single-cloud KMS outage caused a short window of degraded request handling; multipath fallback reduces blast radius while preserving auditability.

What this PR changes (high level): - Adds pkg/rbac/retention_classifier.go that evaluates RBAC v2 attributes and a small rule-set to compute retention_bucket for an event. Rules can be extended via tenant policy YAML. - Adds pkg/kms/multipath.go and pkg/kms/provider_interface.go to support sequential attempts and metrics. - Audit pipeline now tags events with retention_bucket and kms_path (primary|secondary|cache) and emits a retention_decision.trace_id for replayability. - Installer templates updated (cmd/installer/templates/kms-config.yaml) to allow operators to declare primary/secondary KMS endpoints and per-tenant retention overrides. - New integration tests (tests/integration/test_rbac_retention.py, tests/integration/test_kms_multipath.sh) and docs (docs/security/rbac-retention.md)

Design notes and constraints: - Retention classifier is intentionally conservative: if a tenant has no explicit policy, the default is the 'standard' bucket. The classifier is deterministic and pure—no network calls—so it is safe to run inline in the request path. - KMS multipath fallback is limited to retriable errors (timeouts, 5xx from provider). Non-retriable failures (access denied, key not found) do not fall back to avoid policy bypass. - When falling back, the shim records both attempts to the audit stream with an immutable audit envelope and links them via a shared trace id. This preserves non-repudiation requirements for compliance teams.

Backward compatibility & rollout: - No changes to public API surfaces. - Feature gated behind config flags: "rbac_retention.enabled" and "kms.multipath.enabled". Default: both disabled for existing installations. - Migration: installer now includes a one-time migration helper that scans existing audit topics and backfills a retention_bucket="standard" where missing. The helper is provided as a separate CLI: tools/migrate/backfill_retention --topic=...

Testing and verification: - Unit tests for the classifier rules and KMS multipath logic. - Integration tests simulate primary KMS timeout and assert the secondary is tried and audit records contain both attempts. - Per-tenant e2e scenario added to the perf-canary harness to ensure the classifier doesn't add measurable tail-latency under typical workloads.

Security review & notes: - Meera completed a focused security review (SEC-88). Key findings: ensure the fallback does not implicitly change key scope; the multipath provider interface enforces the same key identifier semantics and encryption context checks before usage. - We added an extra audit tag for kms_path and retention_bucket to aid later forensics.

Rollback plan: disable the feature flags and revert installer template entry; no DB schema changes were made, so rollback is safe.

Related: ENG-1329 (retention labels for audit pipeline), SEC-88 (KMS fallback security review).

migration_plan: Run tools/migrate/backfill_retention against audit topics before enabling rbac_retention. Operators should stage secondary KMS endpoints in kms-config.yaml and enable kms.multipath in a canary subset first.
notes_for_ops: If you enable kms.multipath, monitor metric kms_fallback.count and audit retention_decision.*. Set alert if fallback ratio > 0.2 for more than 10m; investigate primary KMS health.
